translations.literal: The Bureau edition reads "jen-wu."
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau edition reads jen-wu.

sentences.zh: 按是月壬午朔，無壬申。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on jen-wu—there was no jen-shen.
translations.idiomatic: That month's new moon was jen-wu—there was no jen-shen.

sentences.zh: 今從局本。

translations.literal: Now follow the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau reading is adopted.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射王球卒 「球」各本並作「琳」，據南史、通鑑改。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Ch'iu died. "Ch'iu": all editions read "Lin"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ch'iu, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, died. "Ch'iu": all editions read "Lin"; corrected from the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 是月 各本並作十二月。

translations.literal: That month. All editions read "twelfth month."
translations.idiomatic: That month. All editions read twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 按上已有十月，十一月，十二月，不當重出十二月。

translations.literal: According to the text above, the tenth, eleventh, and twelfth months have already appeared—it cannot again have a twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: The tenth, eleventh, and twelfth months already appear above—a second twelfth month is impossible.

sentences.zh: 今改作是月。

translations.literal: Now changed to read "that month."
translations.idiomatic: The text is changed to "that month."

sentences.zh: 盛王聖世 「聖」各本並作「祖」，據元龜一九四改。

translations.literal: In a flourishing age of sage rule. "Sage": all editions read "ancestor"; changed according to Yuan Kuei 194.
translations.idiomatic: "In a flourishing age of sage rule." "Sage": all editions read "ancestor"; emended from Yuan Kuei 194.

sentences.zh: 始奉礿祠 「礿」各本並作「初」，據元龜二０七改。

translations.literal: For the first time performing the yü sacrifice. "Yü": all editions read "first"; changed according to Yuan Kuei 207.
translations.idiomatic: "For the first time performing the yü sacrifice." "Yü": all editions read "first"; emended from Yuan Kuei 207.

sentences.zh: 庚申 各本同。

translations.literal: Keng-shen. All editions agree.
translations.idiomatic: Keng-shen. All editions agree.

sentences.zh: 按是月壬申朔，初三日甲戌，是月無庚申。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on jen-shen; the third day was chia-hsu—that month had no keng-shen.
translations.idiomatic: That month's new moon was jen-shen; the third day was chia-hsu—there was no keng-shen in that month.

sentences.zh: 下有甲申，為十三日。

translations.literal: Below there is chia-shen, which is the thirteenth day.
translations.idiomatic: Below comes chia-shen, the thirteenth day.

sentences.zh: 甲戌、甲申之間有庚辰。

translations.literal: Between chia-hsu and chia-shen there is keng-ch'en.
translations.idiomatic: Between chia-hsu and chia-shen stands keng-ch'en.

sentences.zh: 庚申疑庚辰之譌。

translations.literal: Keng-shen is probably a corruption for keng-ch'en.
translations.idiomatic: Keng-shen is probably a scribal error for keng-ch'en.

sentences.zh: 南徐南豫州揚州之浙江西 各本同。

translations.literal: Southern Hsü, Southern Yu, and the region west of the Che River in Yang Province. All editions agree.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Hsü, Southern Yu, and the region west of the Che River in Yang Province. All editions agree.

sentences.zh: 南史於「南徐」下有「南兗」二字。

translations.literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties has the two characters nan-yen after "nan-hsü."
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Southern Dynasties inserts nan-yen after nan-hsü.

sentences.zh: 南豫州刺史武陵王駿加撫軍將軍 「駿」各本作「贊」，三朝本作「諱」。

translations.literal: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling and Governor of Southern Yu Province, was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army. "Chun": all editions read "Tsan"; the Three Dynasties edition reads "hui."
translations.idiomatic: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling and Governor of Southern Yu Province, was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the Army. "Chun": all editions read "Tsan"; the Three Dynasties edition reads "hui."

sentences.zh: 按時武陵王駿，即後之孝武帝。

translations.literal: According to the chronology, at this time it was Prince of Wu-ling Chun—later Emperor Hsiao-wu.
translations.idiomatic: At this date the prince was Wu-ling Chun—the future Emperor Hsiao-wu.

sentences.zh: 贊為宋明帝第九子，後亦封武陵王，時尚未生。

translations.literal: Tsan was the ninth son of Emperor Ming; he too was later enfeoffed as Prince of Wu-ling, but at this time he had not yet been born.
translations.idiomatic: Tsan was the ninth son of Emperor Ming; he too would later be Prince of Wu-ling, but had not yet been born.

sentences.zh: 今改作「駿」。

translations.literal: Now changed to read "Chun."
translations.idiomatic: The text is corrected to Chun.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍南徐州刺史南譙王義宣為車騎將軍荊州刺史 「南徐州刺史」各本並脫「南」字，據義宣傳補。

translations.literal: Yixuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao, General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ching Province. "Governor of Southern Hsü Province": all editions omit the character nan; supplied according to the biography of Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan, Prince of Nan-ch'iao, General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Southern Hsü Province, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Ching Province. "Governor of Southern Hsü Province": all editions omit nan; restored from the biography of Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 九月己未 「己未」各本並作「乙未」，局本作「己未」。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, chi-wei. "Chi-wei": all editions read "i-wei"; the Bureau edition reads "chi-wei."
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, chi-wei. "Chi-wei": all editions read i-wei; the Bureau edition reads chi-wei.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁巳朔，初三日己未，無乙未。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on ting-ssu; the third day was chi-wei—there was no i-wei.
translations.idiomatic: That month's new moon was ting-ssu; the third day was chi-wei—there was no i-wei.

sentences.zh: 今從局本。

translations.literal: Now follow the Bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau reading is adopted.

sentences.zh: 遷漢川流民於沔次 「漢川」各本作「漢州」，按時無「漢州」，據元龜四八六改。

translations.literal: Migrating the Han River displaced persons to the banks at Mien. "Han River": all editions read "Han Prefecture"; at this time there was no "Han Prefecture"—changed according to Yuan Kuei 486.
translations.idiomatic: Resettling Han River refugees on the Mien shore. "Han River": all editions read "Han Prefecture"; there was then no Han Prefecture—emended from Yuan Kuei 486.

sentences.zh: 三月丁巳 下有乙丑。

translations.literal: In the third month, ting-ssu. Below there is i-ch'ou.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, ting-ssu. Below appears i-ch'ou.

sentences.zh: 各本同。

translations.literal: All editions agree.
translations.idiomatic: All editions agree.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，無丁巳，亦無乙丑。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on ting-mao—there was neither ting-ssu nor i-ch'ou.
translations.idiomatic: That month's new moon was ting-mao—neither ting-ssu nor i-ch'ou occurred.

sentences.zh: 四月丙申朔，二十二日丁巳，三十日乙丑。

translations.literal: In the fourth month new moon was on ping-shen; the twenty-second day was ting-ssu; the thirtieth day was i-ch'ou.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth month's new moon was ping-shen; the twenty-second day was ting-ssu; the thirtieth was i-ch'ou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥 各本並作「辛巳」。

translations.literal: Hsin-hai. All editions read "hsin-ssu."
translations.idiomatic: Hsin-hai. All editions read hsin-ssu.

sentences.zh: 通鑑考異云：「按長曆，二月壬辰朔，十日辛丑，二十日辛亥。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror's collation variants say: "According to the long calendar, in the second month new moon was on jen-ch'en; the tenth day was hsin-ch'ou; the twentieth day was hsin-hai.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror's collation variants say: "According to the long calendar, the second month's new moon was jen-ch'en; the tenth day was hsin-ch'ou; the twentieth was hsin-hai.

sentences.zh: 辛巳當作辛亥。

translations.literal: Hsin-ssu should read hsin-hai.
translations.idiomatic: Hsin-ssu should be hsin-hai.

sentences.zh: 」今據改。

translations.literal: " Now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " The text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 安北將軍徐兗二州刺史武陵王駿降號鎮軍將軍 「駿」宋本作「諱」。

translations.literal: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was reduced in rank to General Who Garrisons the Army. "Chun": the Sung edition reads "hui."
translations.idiomatic: Chun, Prince of Wu-ling, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Hsü and Yen provinces, was demoted to General Who Garrisons the Army. "Chun": the Sung edition reads "hui."

sentences.zh: 三朝本、北監本、毛本、殿本作「贊」，今據孝武帝紀訂正。

translations.literal: The Three Dynasties, Northern Directorate, Mao, and Hall editions read "Tsan"; now corrected according to the Annals of Emperor Hsiao-wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties, Northern Directorate, Mao, and Hall editions read Tsan; corrected from the Annals of Emperor Hsiao-wu.

sentences.zh: 說見本卷校勘記第三十條。

translations.literal: The explanation appears in collation note thirty of this scroll.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note thirty in this scroll.

sentences.zh: 五月乙酉亡命司馬順則自號齊王據梁鄒城丁巳婆皇國戊戌河南王並遣使獻方物 按是年五月甲申朔，初二日乙酉，十五日戊戌，無丁巳。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on i-yu, the outlaw Ssu-ma Shun-tse styled himself King of Ch'i and seized Liang-chou city; on ting-ssu the Po-huang state; on wu-hsü the King of Ho-nan—all sent envoys presenting local products. According to the calendar, that year in the fifth month new moon was on chia-shen; the second day was i-yu; the fifteenth day was wu-hsü—there was no ting-ssu.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, i-yu: the outlaw Ssu-ma Shun-tse declared himself King of Ch'i and held Liang-chou city; ting-ssu: the Po-huang state; wu-hsü: the King of Ho-nan—all sent tribute envoys. That year's fifth month had new moon on chia-shen; the second day was i-yu; the fifteenth wu-hsü—there was no ting-ssu.

sentences.zh: 丁巳日支當有誤。

translations.literal: The ting-ssu entry is certainly in error.
translations.idiomatic: The ting-ssu entry must be corrupt.

sentences.zh: 居業未立 「立」各本並作「能」，據元龜一九五改。

translations.literal: Their livelihoods not yet established. "Established": all editions read "able"; changed according to Yuan Kuei 195.
translations.idiomatic: "Their livelihoods not yet established." "Established": all editions read "able"; emended from Yuan Kuei 195.

sentences.zh: 戊午 各本並作「庚午」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Wu-wu. All editions read "keng-wu"; changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Wu-wu. All editions read keng-wu; emended from the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按是月庚戌朔，無庚午。

translations.literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on keng-hsu—there was no keng-wu.
translations.idiomatic: That month's new moon was keng-hsu—there was no keng-wu.

sentences.zh: 初九日戊午。

translations.literal: The ninth day was wu-wu.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth day was wu-wu.
